title: Tell me about a time you had to cut scope or say no
prompt: Tell me about a time you had to reduce scope or explain that a request could not be met as proposed. Explain the constraint, your contribution to the decision and how you communicated it. You can use work, study, volunteering or another responsibility.
blurb: Scope cut / saying no: did they prioritize with clear reasoning and bring people along — or just refuse or overcommit?

rubric.label: Situation & the pressure
rubric.description: Explains the request, the affected people and a specific constraint that required a tradeoff.

rubric.label: Owning the decision
rubric.description: Explains their role in recommending, making or escalating the decision without claiming authority they did not have.

rubric.label: Specific contribution and decisions
rubric.description: Describes the basis for prioritization and a concrete change, alternative or boundary, including what was protected and why.

rubric.label: Outcome and evidence
rubric.description: Describes what happened and how the affected people were informed; agreement or satisfaction from everyone is not required.

rubric.label: Reflection & judgment
rubric.description: Explains an opportunity cost, a condition that would justify revisiting the decision and a lesson about setting expectations.

rubric.label: Clear, relevant communication
rubric.description: Makes the relevant situation, reasoning and contribution understandable in any clear order. No required STAR structure, pronouns, performance of confidence or emotional tone.

reference.scenario: Explore a request that exceeds available time, resources or safe scope. The candidate may recommend a smaller option or involve the authorized decision-maker. Assess justified prioritization and honest communication rather than their ability to obtain approval or avoid disappointment.
model_points: Specifies the request and constraint using available facts.
Clarifies what could be decided personally and what needed approval.
Compares an option or states why a protected requirement cannot be traded away.
Explains the decision or recommendation and a feasible alternative when one exists.
Describes the actual outcome, including disappointment or unresolved approval, without claiming universal agreement.
Identifies what would justify reconsidering scope and what they learned about expectations.

probes.trigger: the reason for the scope decision is unclear
probes.question: Which constraint most affected your choice?
What information or recommendation did you contribute?

probes.trigger: candidate assumes the affected person understood
probes.question: How did you explain the change to them?

red_flags: Promises work they know cannot be delivered without explaining a tradeoff.
Removes an identified safety or essential quality check solely to satisfy pressure.
Presents a recommendation as an approved decision after explaining approval is still pending.
follow_ups: What new information would justify changing that decision?
Which part of the request did you protect?
reference.exemplar_answer: Illustrative example only; it is not a required setting, answer order or achievement standard. Our study group wanted both a survey and interviews for a short assignment. I checked the deadline and estimated that we could analyze one method properly. I proposed keeping the survey and listing interviews as future work, while asking the group to challenge the estimate. We agreed on the smaller scope and explained the limitation in our submission. I learned to state what a smaller plan cannot establish, as well as what it can deliver.
reference.assessment_contract: Assess the selected competency from concrete job-relevant evidence. Examples from paid work, study, volunteering, caregiving, informal work, military service and community activities are equally eligible when relevant. A modest example is sufficient if it shows the competency; employer prestige, formal title and financial scale are not criteria. Accept qualitative or quantitative outcomes supported by the account, including partial or unsuccessful outcomes. Do not require a numeric metric, STAR order, particular pronouns, composure, enthusiasm or a particular communication style. Identify personal contribution by meaning while preserving credit to others. Assess intelligibility and relevance, not accent, fluency, verbosity, visible emotion, disability or private circumstances. Mark genuinely missing evidence not assessed; do not infer poor competence or dishonesty from an absent example. A clearly labeled hypothetical may be discussed as situational practice but must not count as demonstrated past experience. Respect scope of practice, authorization, safety and ethical duties; pausing, declining, reporting or escalating can be sound judgment. Never require obedience, direct confrontation, unpaid overwork or successful persuasion regardless of the circumstances.
